statement: Five numbers have a mean of 20. If one of them is removed, the other four have a mean of 18. If instead a different one of the five is removed, the other four have a mean of 23. What is the difference between the two numbers that were removed?

choices.misconception: I found the difference between the two new means and stopped there.
I multiplied the 5-point difference in means by 5, the original count, instead of by 4.
I only found the first number that was removed.
I only found the second number that was removed.

hints: Turn each mean into a total.
Mean times count gives a total. Subtracting each removed number from the total of all five gives a total of four numbers; compare the two four-number totals.
The five numbers total 100, and the two groups of four total 72 and 92.

solutions.reliable: The five numbers total $5 \times 20 = 100$. Removing the first leaves $4 \times 18 = 72$, so it was 28. Removing the second leaves $4 \times 23 = 92$, so it was 8. The difference is $28 - 8 = 20$. The transferable idea: convert means to totals before adding or removing items.
solutions.elegant: Both groups of four come from the same five numbers, so the difference between the removed numbers equals the difference between the four-number totals: $4 \times (23 - 18) = 20$. The transferable idea: when two cases share the same total, compare their differences directly.

whyOnTest: Means questions test that you convert to totals; this one rewards spotting that only the difference of the two four-number totals matters.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
